source_row.stem: A nurse manager provides minimal direction and allows staff complete autonomy, even in situations requiring more guidance, and a colleague assumes this hands-off approach must actually reflect a values-driven, authentic leadership style. This manager instead demonstrates:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Authentic leadership, a style centered mainly on values-driven transparency rather than on the minimal day-to-day direction this particular manager is actually providing","B":"Servant leadership, a style centered mainly on actively supporting staff needs rather than stepping back entirely from guidance as this manager is actually doing","C":"Transformational leadership, a style centered mainly on inspiring broader change rather than the minimal oversight this particular manager is actually providing","D":"Laissez-faire leadership, appropriate with highly skilled, self-directed teams but risky when more oversight is actually needed"}}
source_row.rationale: Laissez-faire leadership involves minimal direction and maximal staff autonomy, which can work well with highly skilled, self-directed teams but poses risk in situations requiring more active guidance or oversight.
source_row.source_name: Nursing Leadership Foundations — Leadership Style Comparison
